title_en: Read and understand: the five questions
q_en: Can I take any Arabic sentence and work out what it means?
not_yet: Full grammar names and rules: this course taught you to read and understand, not to parse every ending.
Words you have not met: keep a list and look them up, using the root.
Longer texts: use the same five questions, one sentence at a time.
not_yet_ar: أَسْمَاءُ الْقَوَاعِدِ كُلِّهَا: تَعَلَّمْتَ أَنْ تَقْرَأَ وَتَفْهَمَ، لَا أَنْ تُعْرِبَ كُلَّ نِهَايَةٍ.
كَلِمَاتٌ لَمْ تَعْرِفْهَا: اُكْتُبْهَا فِي قَائِمَةٍ وَاطْلُبْهَا بِالْجَذْرِ.
النُّصُوصُ الْأَطْوَلُ: اِسْتَعْمِلِ الْأَسْئِلَةَ الْخَمْسَةَ نَفْسَهَا، جُمْلَةً جُمْلَةً.

slides.why: A student writes لَمْ ذَهَبَ for “did not go”. Wrong! After لَمْ the verb is the present form: لَمْ يَذْهَبْ. (Question 5: how is it joined?)
slides.why_ar: كَتَبَ طَالِبٌ «لَمْ ذَهَبَ». هَذَا خَطَأٌ! بَعْدَ لَمْ يَأْتِي الْفِعْلُ الْمُضَارِعُ: لَمْ يَذْهَبْ.

slides.head_en: I can read Arabic for meaning
slides.big_en: Read. Ask the five questions. Understand.
slides.small: Now do the last exercise: an unseen passage, the five questions, and a Qur’anic verse you have not read.
slides.small_ar: الْآنَ التَّمْرِينُ الْأَخِيرُ: نَصٌّ جَدِيدٌ، وَالْأَسْئِلَةُ الْخَمْسَةُ، وَآيَةٌ لَمْ تَقْرَأْهَا.

can: I can say what kind of word I am looking at (noun, verb or particle).
I can find the root of a word and use it to guess the meaning.
I can tell what a sentence is about and what it says (topic and statement, or verb, doer and object).
I can spot questions, commands and “not” sentences.
I can see how words are joined (prepositions, “and”, “of”, “who/which”, “because”).
I can read a short story or dialogue and answer questions about it.
I can read a short ḥadīth or Qur’anic verse with a gloss and say what it means.
I can read Arabic for meaning.
can_ar: أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَقُولَ مَا نَوْعُ الْكَلِمَةِ (اسْمٌ أَوْ فِعْلٌ أَوْ حَرْفٌ).
أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَجِدَ جَذْرَ الْكَلِمَةِ وَأُخَمِّنَ مَعْنَاهَا.
أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَقُولَ عَنْ مَاذَا الْجُمْلَةُ وَمَاذَا تَقُولُ (مُبْتَدَأٌ وَخَبَرٌ أَوْ فِعْلٌ وَفَاعِلٌ وَمَفْعُولٌ).
أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَعْرِفَ الْأَسْئِلَةَ وَالْأَوَامِرَ وَجُمَلَ النَّفْيِ.
أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَرَى كَيْفَ تَرْتَبِطُ الْكَلِمَاتُ (حُرُوفُ الْجَرِّ وَالْوَاوُ وَالْإِضَافَةُ وَ«الَّذِي» وَ«لِأَنَّ»).
أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَقْرَأَ قِصَّةً قَصِيرَةً أَوْ حِوَارًا وَأُجِيبَ عَنِ الْأَسْئِلَةِ.
أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَقْرَأَ حَدِيثًا قَصِيرًا أَوْ آيَةً مَعَ الشَّرْحِ وَأَقُولَ مَعْنَاهَا.

sections.name: A
sections.en: A passage you have not seen: the night of the mawlid. Read it aloud once all the way through. Then answer.
lines: فِي لَيْلَةِ الْمَوْلِدِ ذَهَبَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ أَخِيهِ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ.
On the night of the mawlid the boy went with his brother to the mosque.
دَخَلَ الْوَلَدُ الْمَجْلِسَ الَّذِي فِي الرِّبَاطِ.
The boy entered the majlis that is in the ribāṭ.
سَأَلَ الْحَبِيبُ الْوَلَدَ: هَلْ قَرَأْتَ هَذَا الْكِتَابَ؟
The Habib asked the boy: Have you read this book?
قَالَ الْوَلَدُ: لَا، لَمْ أَقْرَأْهُ، لَكِنْ أَنَا أَطْلُبُهُ.
The boy said: No, I have not read it, but I am looking for it.
قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: اِقْرَأْهُ، فَإِنَّ فِيهِ دَرْسًا جَيِّدًا.
The Habib said: Read it, for there is a good lesson in it.
وَقَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ الْمَوْلِدَ مَعَ ثَلَاثَةِ طُلَّابٍ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ.
And the boy read the mawlid with three students in the majlis.
رَجَعَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ، وَلَمْ يَجْلِسْ فِي الشَّارِعِ.
The boy returned to the house, and he did not sit in the street.
سَأَلَتْهُ أُمُّهُ: مَاذَا فَعَلْتَ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ؟
His mother asked him: What did you do in the mosque?
قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ كُلَّ كَلِمَةٍ طَيِّبَةٍ فِي الْمَوْلِدِ.
He said: I heard every good word at the mawlid.
His mother thanked him because he is a good boy.

sections.name: X
lines: A boy went to a mosque.
The boy sat in the mosque.
The boy opened a muṣḥaf (a copy of the Qur’an).
The boy read in the muṣḥaf.
The boy sat in the study circle.
The friends went to the mosque.
The students read in the books.
The Habib sat in the mosque.
The Habib is a righteous man.
Is the Habib in the mosque?
Yes, the Habib is in the mosque.
The boy came in through the door.
The mother looked at the boy.
The boy sits in the study circle today.
Maryam is reading the muṣḥaf now.
The boy was happy in the majlis.
Maryam was happy in the study circle.
The boy did not leave the majlis.
لَنْ يَجْلِسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْبَيْتِ غَدًا.
The boy will not sit at home tomorrow.
ذَهَبَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْأَبِ إِلَى الزِّيَارَةِ.
The boy went with the father to the ziyāra (the visit).
The boy sat with good manners in the majlis.
The boy heard the Rātib (the litany) with his father.
ذَهَبَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الصَّبَاحِ إِلَى بَيْتِ الْحَبِيبِ.
The boy went in the morning to the Habib’s house.
The boy sat in the circle of dhikr (remembrance of Allah).
The Habib asked him about the lesson.
The boy served the guests and carried the food.
ثُمَّ جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْحَبِيبِ وَسَمِعَ الدَّرْسَ.
Then the boy sat with the Habib and heard the lesson.
The guests thanked the boy who served them.
حَفِظَ الْوَلَدُ مَا سَمِعَ مِنَ الْحَبِيبِ.
The boy memorised what he heard from the Habib.
فَهِمَ الْوَلَدُ الدَّرْسَ لِأَنَّهُ خَدَمَ الضُّيُوفَ.
The boy understood the lesson because he served the guests.
فِي الْمَجْلِسِ خَمْسَةُ ضُيُوفٍ وَسَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ كُلَّ كَلِمَةٍ.
There are five guests in the majlis, and the boy heard every word.
جَاءَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الرِّبَاطِ فِي الصَّبَاحِ.
The boy came to the ribāṭ in the morning.
The Habib said: Knowledge is light.
سَأَلَ عُمَرُ صَدِيقَهُ: هَلْ أَنْتَ ذَاهِبٌ إِلَى الرَّوْحَةِ؟
Umar asked his friend: Are you going to the rawḥa?
سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ مِنَ الْحَبِيبِ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: الصَّلَاةُ نُورٌ.
The boy heard from the Habib: The Prophet ﷺ said: Prayer is light.
The boy opened his muṣḥaf and read his wird (his daily portion).
صَلَّى الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الطُّلَّابِ ثُمَّ دَعَا.
The boy prayed with the students, then made duʿāʾ.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ الْمَوْلِدَ لِأَنَّ مَحَبَّةَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ فِي قَلْبِهِ.
The boy read the mawlid because love of the Prophet ﷺ is in his heart.

It joins: it gives the reason (“because”).

items.en: Questions 1 and 2: kind of word and root?
Who read the mawlid, and why?
items.model: The boy (الْوَلَدُ), because love of the Prophet ﷺ is in his heart.

items.en: Read the whole story strip once more. Where did the boy begin, and what had he become by the end?
items.model: At a mosque, a small boy with a muṣḥaf; a student who serves, learns and loves the Prophet ﷺ.
